title: LatticeMind: A Validation-Gated Agentic Framework for Density Functional Theory Workflows
authors: Nathaniel M. Vegh, Yu Zhu, Rapha\"el J. Prentki, F\'elix Beaudoin, Shuaishuai Yuan, Hong Guo
abstract: arXiv:2610.26869v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: First-principles calculations are rarely single solver calls: they are multistage workflows in which structures, settings, and saved densities must pass correctly between dependent stages. Language models can write a valid single input, but reliability collapses once stages are chained: a dropped dependency, wrong file handoff, or hallucinated keyword can invalidate results even when the solver runs, and such errors surface only after costly execution. We introduce LatticeMind, a validation-gated agentic framework that converts natural-language requests into executable, checkable density functional theory (DFT) projects. A workflow contract specifies required stages, files, and dependencies; deterministic validators inspect the project before any solver launch; failed checks trigger bounded repair; and reports remain traceable to project files. On a 44-case RESCU benchmark spanning total-energy, density-of-states, band-structure, magnetic, phonon workflows, three non-flagship LLM backends reproduced every reference value; 119 of 132 runs passed on the first validated plan and the rest after one repair cycle. Ablations identify the workflow contract and pre-execution validation as the principal reliability mechanisms; a conventional trial-and-repair baseline reaches 71% at twice the token cost per success. The same architecture reproduces every reference value on a 19-case VASP benchmark, demonstrating transfer across solvers. Beyond these task families, LatticeMind generated and validated the 23 inputs of a multistage study of Rh-induced electronic responses at a Rh$_6$/In$_x$Ga$_{1-x}$N photocatalyst interface. These results establish workflow contracts, deterministic validation, bounded repair, and traceable records as a practical foundation for reliable AI-assisted scientific computing, where preventable errors are caught before execution and the solver is never the first validator.
summary:
- LatticeMind converts natural‑language requests into executable DFT workflows, using deterministic pre‑execution validators and bounded repair to ensure correct file handoffs and dependencies.
- On 44 RESCU and 19 VASP benchmarks, it reproduces every reference value, with 119/132 runs passing on the first validated plan and the rest after a single repair cycle.
- Ablations reveal that the workflow contract and pre‑execution validation are the primary reliability mechanisms, outperforming a conventional trial‑and‑repair baseline.

title: Vortex matter as a magnetically programmable metasurface for tuning near-field radiative heat transfer
authors: Siddharth Sangi, Pramod Reddy, Shanhui Fan
abstract: arXiv:2610.26874v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Near-field radiative heat transfer (NFRHT) is of great interest for energy conversion and thermal management. Recent work on NFRHT has shown that metasurfaces can enhance NFRHT and reshape its spectral characteristics. Here, we show that the vortex lattice of a type-II superconductor represents a self-assembled metasurface whose lattice dimensions, in contrast to most other metasurfaces, can be tuned by magnetic fields, allowing NFRHT to be varied by orders of magnitude. Specifically, we show that for two Nb surfaces at 4.2 K and separated by a 100 nm gap, NFRHT can be magnetically tuned by a factor >200. Further, we show that the tuning range grows upon cooling, exceeding 10^5 at 2 K, which is far beyond the order-unity modulation of many proposed schemes for tuning NFRHT. Our results establish vortex matter as a magnetically programmable thermal metasurface and open new opportunities for tuning the flow of heat at the nanoscale.
summary:
- Vortex lattice of a type‑II superconductor serves as a self‑assembled, magnetically tunable metasurface.
- Magnetic field changes near‑field radiative heat transfer between two Nb surfaces (2 K, 100 nm gap) by >200×; at 2 K the modulation exceeds 10⁵×.
- Establishes vortex matter as a magnetically programmable thermal metasurface, enabling large‑range nanoscale heat flow control.

title: High-Field and Light-Dependent Magnetization Provides Evidence for Coexisting Granular Superconductivity and Superparamagnetism in Nitrogen-Doped Diamond
authors: E. Osmic, J. Barzola-Quiquia, S. Winnerl, T. Herrmannsdoerfer, M. Uhlarz, J. Meijer
abstract: arXiv:2610.26880v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigated the field-, temperature-, and time-dependent magnetic moment of a nitrogen-doped type Ib diamond in darkness and under monochromatic light with a low laser intensity of about 160 $\mu$W cm$^{-2}$. In darkness, below approximately 25 K, the magnetic moment exhibits unconventional hysteresis loops that can be explained by the coexistence of superparamagnetism and superconductivity in certain regions of the sample. Under illumination, this hysteresis largely disappears, leaving mainly the superparamagnetic contribution. Temperature-dependent measurements reveal an irreversibility below 25 K in darkness, which vanishes under illumination. Similarly, at 0.5 T and below 25 K, the time-dependent magnetization shows flux-creep-like behavior that disappears when the sample is illuminated. All light-induced changes are fully reversible: the magnetic properties measured in darkness are restored after the sample is heated above roughly 50 K. Removing the superparamagnetic contribution from magnetization measurements up to $\pm 14$ T reveals clear characteristics of a granular superconductor, namely, a well-defined penetration field $H_p \approx 2.6$ T and a critical field $H_{c2} \approx 10.6$ T. Based on theoretical considerations, we attribute the observed phenomena to the combined effects of internal stress and local variations in nitrogen concentration within localized regions that can be regarded as grains. This interpretation is supported by Raman and birefringence spectroscopy measurements on the same sample.
summary:
- Nitrogen‑doped diamond shows coexisting superparamagnetism and granular superconductivity below ~25 K, revealed by hysteresis loops and flux‑creep‑like time dependence.
- Low‑intensity illumination (~160 µW cm⁻²) suppresses the superconducting contribution, leaving only superparamagnetism; the effect reverses when heated above ~50 K.
- After removing the superparamagnetic part, the superconducting phase displays a penetration field Hp ≈ 6 T and upper critical field Hc2

title: Zeeman Quantum Geometry of the Layer Pseudo-spin
abstract: arXiv:2610.26982v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two-dimensional layers coupled by position-dependent interlayer tunnelling host a layer pseudo-spin whose polarization is a controllable internal degree of freedom. We introduce the quantum geometry of this layer pseudo-spin: a mixed tensor formed from the interband Berry connection and the layer matrix element, which governs the response to an oscillating in-plane electric field. Because the layer pseudo-spin is an Ising-type scalar invariant under threefold rotation, its selection rules differ from those of a pseudovector spin. In a minimal two-band model, the layer-pseudo-spin quantum metric and Zeeman--Berry curvature are nonzero, while their zone integrals vanish. An in-plane drive therefore leaves the spatially averaged polarization unchanged at linear order but imprints a moir\'{e}-periodic intracell pattern, directly imageable by layer-resolved tunnelling. For twisted MoTe$_2$ bilayer, we quantify the local dipole modulation and identify the rectified, helicity-odd, and third-harmonic channels through which a net response appears at higher order.
summary:
- Defines a mixed tensor of interband Berry connection and layer matrix element that describes the quantum geometry of layer pseudo‑spin and its response to in‑plane electric fields.
- Shows that in a minimal two‑band model the quantum metric and Zeeman–Berry curvature are nonzero yet their Brillouin‑zone integrals vanish, so a linear drive produces only a moiré‑periodic intracell polarization pattern.
- Quantifies local dipole modulation in twisted MoTe₂ bilayers and identifies rectified, helicity‑odd, and third‑harmonic channels that generate a net higher‑order response.

title: Tailoring Dielectric Relaxation and Charge Transport in Amorphous Ge-Te-Se Phase-Change Materials through Yttrium Incorporation
authors: Surbhi Agarwal, Ji\v{r}\'i Vac\'ik, D. K. Dwivedi
abstract: arXiv:2610.26996v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Te(1-x)(GeSe0.5)Yx (x = 0.05, 0.10, 0.15) alloys were prepared by a melt-quenching method and characterized using dielectric spectroscopy. The dielectric parameters and electrical conductivity were evaluated to assess their potential for phase-change memory and other electronic applications. The temperature and frequency dependence of the dielectric constants, ac conductivity, and dielectric loss of prepared chalcogenide glassy alloys were investigated over the frequency range 1 Hz - 1 MHz, and the temperature range 302 - 422 K, below the glass transition temperature. Both dielectric loss and dielectric constant were found to decrease with increasing frequency and decreasing temperature. The observed dielectric loss change was interpreted using the Guintini model of dielectric dispersion, correlated barrier hopping (CBH) model, and orientation polarization. The Cole-Cole analysis confirmed a distribution of relaxation times and yielded activation energies consistent with the CBH conduction mechanism. The frequency dependence of the ac conductivity follows the power law (A{\omega}s), where the frequency exponent (s < 1) decreases with increasing temperature, further supporting the CBH conduction mechanism. The incorporation of Y increases the density of localized tail states, resulting in enhanced ac conductivity. These findings suggest that the investigated materials are promising candidates for future phase-change memory and other electronic device applications.
summary:
- Yttrium incorporation raises localized tail states, enhancing ac conductivity while reducing dielectric constant and loss with frequency/temperature.
- Dielectric relaxation fits Guintini, CBH, and orientation polarization models; Cole‑Cole analysis confirms distributed relaxation times and CBH activation energies.
- Ac conductivity follows σ∝ω^s (s < with s decreasing as temperature rises, supporting CBH conduction and indicating promise for phase‑change memory applications.

title: Achieving ultrahigh-temperature superfluidity in atomic Fermi gases by suppressing pairing fluctuations
abstract: arXiv:2610.26997v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Achieving room-temperature superconductivity has been a long-sought goal of both the physics community and the industry. The superfluid transition temperature $T_\mathrm{c}$ of a Fermi system initially increases with increasing pairing strength between fermions following the mean-field prediction of the Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) theory, and is then suppressed by pairing fluctuations as the strength increases further, which prevents $T_\mathrm{c}$ from becoming high. Here we propose a mechanism for suppressing pairing fluctuations using the synergy between population imbalance and momentum space confinement in lattice systems, enabling an ultrahigh $T_\mathrm{c}$ at moderately strong attraction. We show that in a three-dimensional optical lattice, strong Pauli exclusion between paired and excess majority fermions pushes up the pair excitation energy and suppresses finite-momentum pairing fluctuations. The mechanism is general to any lattice with a finite Brillouin zone; the optimal imbalance is modest ($p\lesssim 0.1$), keeping the Zeeman field small and avoiding orbital complications. The gapped pair dispersion at moderate imbalance exponentially suppresses thermal condensate depletion, providing a testable signature. The gapped dispersion, enhanced condensate fraction, and pseudogap reduction are all accessible in present-day experiments. This work opens new avenues toward room-temperature superconductivity.
summary:
- Population imbalance combined with lattice momentum confinement suppresses pairing fluctuations, boosting the superfluid transition temperature.
- Pauli exclusion between paired and excess fermions in a 3D optical lattice raises pair excitation energy, creating a gapped pair dispersion that exponentially reduces thermal condensate depletion.
- The effect is optimal at modest imbalance (p ≲ , yielding an enhanced condensate fraction, reduced pseudogap, and experimentally accessible signatures toward room‑temperature superconductivity.

title: Heat-current-induced nonreciprocal phonon damping
authors: Tingwei Deng, Xianyong Ding, Rui Wang, Xiangang Wan
abstract: arXiv:2610.27014v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time-reversal symmetry enforces equal equilibrium linewidths for time-reversed phonon modes at opposite wave vectors. Here we show that a steady heat current can produce nonreciprocal anharmonic damping even in centrosymmetric nonmagnetic crystals. The effect arises from nonequilibrium occupations of scattering partners, which change the statistical weights of time-reversed three-phonon channels while their squared matrix elements remain equal. Within the single-mode relaxation-time approximation, we derive a linewidth correction that is linear in the temperature gradient and odd under wave-vector reversal. The response depends on scattering-partner velocities and equilibrium lifetimes and retains signed channel weights absent from the equilibrium linewidth. First-principles calculations for centrosymmetric MgO and diamond yield nonzero, mode-dependent linewidth corrections at selected finite wave vectors, demonstrating the mechanism in both ionic and covalent crystals. Reversing the heat current at fixed local temperature exchanges the broadening and narrowing of paired modes. This current-reversible linewidth contrast provides a spectral signature of occupation feedback, with potential implications for nonlinear phonon transport.
summary:
- Heat current induces nonreciprocal anharmonic phonon damping in centrosymmetric nonmagnetic crystals.
- Linewidth correction is linear in the temperature gradient and odd under wave‑vector reversal.
- First‑principles MgO and diamond calculations show mode‑dependent corrections; reversing the heat current swaps broadening and narrowing.

title: MOFFieldBench: A Machine Learning Benchmark for Continuous Electronic Fields in Metal-Organic Frameworks
authors: Zhaolin Hu, Hehe Fan, Chenhao Rao, Wangyihan Guo, Meng Xu, Qiwei Yang, Yi Yang
abstract: arXiv:2610.27036v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine-learning models for metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) predominantly rely on atomic structures, whereas electron-density (ED) and electrostatic-potential (ESP) fields remain underexplored as scalable learning representations. These continuous fields encode complementary spatial and electronic information relevant to structure-property relationships, particularly pore geometry and guest-framework interactions, but costly first-principles calculations, storage requirements and the scarcity of systematically aligned datasets limit their broader use. Here we introduce MOFFieldBench, a multimodal benchmark comprising approximately 46,000 MOFs with one-to-one aligned crystallographic structures, ED fields and ESP fields. A unified workflow integrates field generation, error-controlled compression and sparse point-cloud representation, supporting field reconstruction, prediction of 13 material properties, multimodal property prediction and pairwise cross-modal retrieval. ED and ESP provide competitive representations for pore geometry, adsorption and separation properties. Multimodal fusion improves several prediction tasks relative to the best unimodal reference, supporting complementary predictive roles for atomic structures and electronic fields. Learned ED reconstruction closely approximates first-principles reference densities, while predicted-density initialization reduces self-consistent-field calculation time by 13.59\% on average in paired tests. These results support electronic fields as practical, informative learning modalities and establish MOFFieldBench as a resource for studying representation choice, multimodal learning and electronic-field-driven MOF modelling.
summary:
- MOFFieldBench supplies ~46 k MOFs with aligned crystal, ED, and ESP fields for scalable ML on continuous electronic representations.
- ED/ESP fields match or surpass atomic structures in predicting pore geometry, adsorption, and separation; multimodal fusion yields further gains.
- Workflow enables field compression, sparse point‑clouds, and learned ED reconstruction, cutting SCF calculation time by ~6 %.

title: Field Theory of the Gutzwiller Projection
authors: Abhijat Sarma, Cenke Xu, Chong Wang
abstract: arXiv:2610.27050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Gutzwiller projection produces a well-known ansatz for spin-liquid and quantum Hall ground-state wavefunctions that is amenable to numerical simulation, with the Laughlin wavefunction being the most celebrated example. A long-standing issue is the precise relation between the Gutzwiller projection and the closely related parton gauge theory. Here, we clarify this issue by providing a field-theoretic description of the Gutzwiller projection. In a path integral description, the universal physics of the projected state is described in terms of a gauge field supported on a temporal slab of vanishing width $\epsilon \rightarrow 0$ coupled to the bulk matter fields. We analytically derive the universal physics of various Gutzwiller projected states. Our construction is also applicable to discrete symmetries, and we use it to analyze various projected SPT states. Among our results, we show that the Gutzwiller projection is not a good ansatz for the long-distance properties of $U(1)$ Dirac spin liquids, spinon Fermi surface spin liquids or composite Fermi liquids, and that the Gutzwiller projection of a quantum spin Hall state has only quasi-long range order. In contrast, in examples where the gauge field is gapped, including Laughlin states, $\mathbb{Z}_2$ spin liquids and Luttinger liquids, we show that the slab gauge theory from Gutzwiller projection reproduces the correct universal physics of the full parton gauge theory. We also present a generalization of our field theory that describes $G$-intertwining defects, with application to self-duality defects of recent theoretical interest.
summary:
- Field‑theoretic description of Gutzwiller projection as a gauge field on a vanishing‑width temporal slab.
- Works for gapped phases (Laughlin, ℤ₂ spin liquids, Luttinger liquids) but fails to capture long‑distance physics of gapless U(Dirac, spinon Fermi surface, or composite Fermi liquids.
- Extends to discrete symmetries and projected SPTs, showing only quasi‑long‑range order in the projected quantum spin Hall state.

title: Spectral signatures of hidden order and hidden quantum critical points
authors: Reja H. Wilke, Henning Schl\"omer, Sebastian Paeckel, Annabelle Bohrdt, Fabian Grusdt
abstract: arXiv:2610.27060v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hidden-order phases elude the conventional Ginzburg-Landau framework: although they spontaneously break symmetry, their order remains invisible to standard local two-point correlators. Instead, they are typically characterized by nonlocal (string) order parameters and are believed to underlie a range of exotic quantum states, such as symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases. While hidden correlations have previously been detected through nonlocal observables in quantum gas microscope experiments, in realistic solid-state systems multipoint observables are typically inaccessible and the signatures of hidden order remain largely unexplored. In this work, we show that hidden order in doped spin chains can be directly probed through dynamical two-point response functions measurable by resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) and neutron scattering. Focusing on a minimal model, we numerically identify clear spectral fingerprints of both the hidden-order phase, its associated hidden quantum critical point as well as a specific group of gapless SPT phases. Complementing our numerical results with analytical insights, we uncover the microscopic origin of these spectral signatures and demonstrate how they emerge from the interplay between spin and charge degrees of freedom. Together, our results establish spectroscopy as a practical probe of hidden order and gapless SPT phases and provide a unified understanding of the low-energy physics governing these unconventional quantum phases.
summary:
- Hidden order in doped spin chains shows up as distinct features in dynamical two‑point spectra measurable by RIXS and neutron scattering.
- Numerical and analytical work identifies clear spectral fingerprints of the hidden‑order phase, its hidden quantum critical point, and gapless SPT phases.
- Spectroscopy therefore offers a practical probe of nonlocal order and gapless SPT behavior in solid‑state systems.

title: Chiral magnetic excitations in the RMn6Sn6 kagome metals (R=Tb, Ho, Er, and Y)
authors: Christopher J. Ranlett (Ames National Laboratory, Iowa State University Department of Physics and Astronomy), Tianxiong Han (Ames National Laboratory, Iowa State University Department of Physics and Astronomy), S. X. M. Riberolles (Ames National Laboratory), Dhurba R. Jaishi (Ames National Laboratory, Iowa State University Department of Physics and Astronomy), Tyler J. Slade (Ames National Laboratory), Bing Li (European Spallation Source ERIC), A. Sapkota (Ames National Laboratory), D. L. Abernathy (Oak Ridge National Laboratory Neutron Scattering Division), Rebecca L. Dally (National Institute of Standards and Technology Physical Measurement Laboratory Sensor Science Division), J. W. Lynn (National Institute of Standards and Technology Center for Neutron Research), B. G. Ueland (Ames National Laboratory), R. J. McQueeney (Ames National Laboratory, Iowa State University Department of Physics and Astronomy)
abstract: arXiv:2610.27430v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent inelastic neutron scattering (INS) investigations of the kagome metal TbMn6Sn6 reveal novel chiral magnetic excitations associated with the kagome layer. These excitations appear to have an itinerant character with a large energy scale (> 100 meV) and heavy damping; however, the origin of these excitations, which are not predicted by local moment linear spin-wave theory, is not understood. Here, we use INS to show that chiral excitations are also found in RMn6Sn6 compounds with R=Tb, Ho, Er, and Y having uniaxial, tilted, planar ferrimagnet, and planar double-spiral magnetic structures, respectively. Thus, the chiral excitations exist regardless of the magnetic structure. Additionally, R=Er and Y demonstrate that the chiral mode intensity is weaker in planar magnetic structures, suggesting that excitations are transverse to the local Mn moment direction. The chiral excitations appear only at L=odd positions in the Brilloun zone, and correspond to chiral spin exciations of the same handedness within each kagome layer, and pi out-of-phase between layers.
summary:
- Chiral magnetic excitations detected in all RMn₆Sn₆ kagome metals (R = Tb, Ho, Er, Y) by inelastic neutron scattering.
- Excitations are itinerant, >100 meV, heavily damped, appear only at odd L positions, with identical handedness within layers and π‑phase between layers.
- Intensity is reduced in planar magnetic structures (Er, Y), suggesting excitations transverse to the local Mn moment direction.

title: Finite-temperature spectral functions of lattice polarons with process tensors
abstract: arXiv:2610.27582v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a process tensor approach for calculating the finite-temperature spectral functions of lattice polarons. We show that the finite-temperature phonon influence functional can be expressed as the elementwise exponential of a low-rank matrix product state, enabling an efficient summation of electron worldlines. An embedding construction embeds worldlines of different propagation times into a single matrix product state. This construction yields the propagator over the full simulated time interval in a single calculation. We benchmark this approach against available finite-temperature density-matrix renormalization group results for the one-dimensional Holstein polaron. We further obtain numerically converged spectra for the two-dimensional Holstein polaron. The spectra reveal a progressive transfer of spectral weight from coherent spectral features into an incoherent background with increasing temperature.
summary:
- Developed a process‑tensor method that expresses the finite‑temperature phonon influence functional as an elementwise exponential of a low‑rank matrix‑product state, enabling efficient electron worldline summation.
- Introduced an embedding that unifies worldlines of different propagation times into a single matrix‑product state, producing the full propagator in one calculation; benchmarked against 1D Holstein polaron DMRG and extended to converged 2D spectra.
- Showed that increasing temperature transfers spectral weight from coherent peaks to an incoherent background in Holstein polaron spectral functions.

title: Orbital Magnetization within Self-Consistent Hartree-Fock via an Envelope Theorem
abstract: arXiv:2610.27624v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Orbital magnetization is an elementary thermodynamic response function of a quantum system: the derivative of the grand potential with respect to magnetic field. However, naive perturbation theory is fraught with difficulties, as even infinitesimal magnetic fields shatter any bands into a Hofstadter butterfly spectrum. Even at the self-consistent Hartree-Fock (mean field) level, rigorous formulas for the orbital magnetization have only become available within the last year. This work provides a straightforward derivation of orbital magnetization at the mean field level using a completely real-space approach. The key tools used are the magnetic perturbation theory developed in the 1960s and an envelope theorem, which is a standard result in the calculus of variations. For simplicity, we restrict to insulating states at zero temperature on the infinite plane. We also discuss the natural connections to projected position operators and quantum geometry, as well as practical numerical computations.
summary:
- Derives orbital magnetization for self‑consistent Hartree–Fock using real‑space magnetic perturbation theory and an envelope theorem.
- Applies to insulating, zero‑temperature systems on an infinite plane, avoiding Hofstadter butterfly complications.
- Connects the result to projected position operators, quantum geometry, and outlines numerical implementation.

title: Persistent Photo-Enhancement of Molecular Orbital Excitations in the Kondo Insulator FeSb$_2$
authors: Ke-Jun Xu, Nathan Giles-Donovan, Paulina Majchrzak, Abhi Suthar, Matthias Hepting, Marco Trento, Giacomo Ghiringhelli, Elizabeth Skoropata, Hiroki Ueda, Eugenio Paris, Biaolong Liu, Elia Razzoli, Wei-Sheng Lee, Thomas P. Devereaux, Zhi-Xun Shen, Dung-Hai Lee, Robert J. Birgeneau
abstract: arXiv:2610.27630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When insulators are excited by photons with above-gap energies, photo-doped carriers are transiently generated. Typically, orbital excitations weaken and broaden due to increased screening by these transient carriers, followed by a few-ps recovery via phonon thermalization. Here we report the observation of anomalous dynamics of many-body molecular orbital excitations in the narrow-gap Kondo insulator FeSb$_2$. In the pumped X-ray absorption spectra following excitation with 1~$\mu$m photons, we observe a transient transfer of absorption intensity from the delocalized states at the main absorption peak to the localized molecular orbital states at the pre-edge. At the resonance of the low-energy molecular orbital excitations, the pumped resonant inelastic X-ray spectra show an approximately 30\% intensity increase at a pump fluence of 11 mJ/cm$^2$ concomitant with the emergence of an energy gain feature. While the energy gain feature disappears after about 1-2~ps, the increased molecular orbital excitation intensities partially persist for at least 50~ps with no discernible energy shift. These observations require the invocation of a many-body excitation picture beyond single particle population changes.

title: Lattice symmetry breaking and strain control of single-$\mathbf{q}$ magnetism in Na$_3$Co$_2$SbO$_6$
authors: Yuchen Gu, Wu Xie, Xintong Li, Junhong Liu, Xianghong Jin, Dmitry Khalyavin, Fabio Orlandi, Pascal Manuel, Ping Miao, Yuan Li
abstract: arXiv:2610.27663v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distinguishing single-$\mathbf{q}$ from multi-$\mathbf{q}$ magnetism constrains microscopic spin Hamiltonians. Here we determine the ground state of the candidate Kitaev magnet Na$_3$Co$_2$SbO$_6$ through its coupling to the lattice. High-resolution neutron diffraction reveals a spontaneous monoclinic-to-triclinic distortion at the magnetic transition, in contrast to the absence of detectable lattice-symmetry breaking in triple-$\mathbf{q}$ Na$_2$Co$_2$TeO$_6$. Together with strain-selective magnetic responses, this identifies single-$\mathbf{q}$ order in Na$_3$Co$_2$SbO$_6$ over the proposed symmetry-preserving double-$\mathbf{q}$ state. Uniaxial compression along a low-symmetry in-plane direction achieves the domain selection that magnetic-field training could not, revealing the intrinsic field-induced phase boundaries of the dominant domain. These results establish strain as a symmetry-conjugate field for magnetic domains and highlight magnetoelastic coupling as a route to diagnose, manipulate, and potentially tune magnetic states.
summary:
- Monoclinic‑to‑triclinic lattice distortion at the magnetic transition confirms single‑q order in Na₃Co₂SbO₆.
- Uniaxial strain along a low‑symmetry in‑plane axis selects magnetic domains and exposes intrinsic field‑induced phase boundaries.
- Magnetoelastic coupling serves as a symmetry‑conjugate field to diagnose, manipulate, and tune magnetic states, distinguishing single‑q from multi‑q magnetism.

title: Symmetry Enriched Criticality from Kennedy Tasaki Self-Duality
authors: Mingyuan Chen, Sheng Yang, Xue-Jia Yu
abstract: arXiv:2610.27666v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The interplay between topology and quantum criticality has established symmetry enriched criticality as a new paradigm beyond conventional frameworks in condensed matter and statistical physics. However, the conditions under which such criticality emerges remain poorly understood. In this work, we show that a broad class of symmetry enriched critical points separating symmetry protected topological (SPT) and spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB) phases is governed by Kennedy Tasaki (KT) self duality. At these criticalities, the KT transformation that interchanges the SPT and SSB phases acts as a self-dual noninvertible symmetry, endowing the critical points with nontrivial topological characteristics. We numerically demonstrate this mechanism in $\mathbb{Z}_{n} \times \mathbb{Z}_{n}$ cluster qudit chains and further argue that it naturally extends to higher dimensions, providing a duality based criterion for identifying symmetry-enriched criticality across dimensions.
summary:
- Symmetry‑enriched critical points between SPT and SSB phases are governed by Kennedy–Tasaki self‑duality, a noninvertible self‑dual symmetry.
- The KT transformation swaps SPT and SSB phases, giving the critical points nontrivial topological features.
- Numerical results on $\mathbb{Z}_n\times\mathbb{Z}_n$ cluster qudit chains confirm the mechanism, and a duality criterion extends to higher dimensions.

title: Good-$\Gamma$ Numbers: A Shell-Optimized Route to the Thermodynamic Limit in Quantum Monte Carlo Calculations of the High-Density Two-Dimensional Electron Gas
authors: S. Azadi, T. D. K\"{u}hne, A. Principi, M. S. Bahramy
abstract: arXiv:2610.27761v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Single-particle finite-size errors remain a central obstacle in quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations of periodic systems, conventionally reduced via twist averaging (TA). Here we introduce Good-$\Gamma$ (GG) particle numbers as system sizes $N$ at which the $\Gamma$-point Hartree--Fock (HF) energy of the high-density two-dimensional uniform electron gas (2D UEG) lies anomalously close to its thermodynamic-limit (TL) value. All results in this work concern the 2D UEG in its high-density Fermi-liquid regime, $r_s=1$--$4$. We systematically investigate the kinetic- and exchange-energy errors, $\Delta KE(N)$ and $\Delta EX(N)$, that underlie this one-body finite-size-error cancellation across four densities and both spin polarizations. We then compare diffusion Monte Carlo (DMC) energies extrapolated to the TL from GG-$N$ sequences against twist-averaged extrapolations at the same densities and polarizations, finding agreement to within a fraction of a millihartree in every case, independent of whether a $1/N$ or an $N^{-5/4}$ extrapolation form is used.
summary:
- Good‑Γ particle numbers make the Γ‑point Hartree–Fock energy of the high‑density 2D UEG almost equal to its thermodynamic‑limit value, cutting single‑particle finite‑size errors.
- Kinetic‑ and exchange‑energy errors are systematically studied for \(r_s=1\)–4 and both spin polarizations, revealing cancellation at Good‑Γ sizes.
- Diffusion‑Monte‑Carlo energies extrapolated from Good‑Γ sequences match twist‑averaged extrapolations within < 1 mHartree, independent of \(1/N\) or \(N^{-5/4}\) fitting.

title: Spin fluctuations and nearly isotropic quasiparticles in the doped three-dimensional Hubbard model
authors: Pengcheng Hou, Kun Chen, Youjin Deng
abstract: arXiv:2610.27779v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Away from half filling and above its Neel temperature, the three-dimensional Hubbard model is a paramagnetic metal with antiferromagnetic spin fluctuations, where controlled momentum-resolved results have been lacking. Using connected-determinant diagrammatic Monte Carlo, we compute the momentum-resolved self-energy for n = 0.4-0.95, T/t = 0.05-0.33 and U/t = 4-8, and the full-zone spin susceptibility at twelve of these points, focusing on U/t = 4. At U/t = 4 and toward half filling the spin fluctuations become strong: for n = 0.7-0.9 at T/t = 0.14 they enhance the susceptibility peak up to sevenfold and raise the momentum-dependent part of the scattering rate to four to five times its second-order value. They are driven by an effective spin interaction screened to about 2U/3 and nearly uniform over the zone. Yet the peak height is set by the slightly smaller value of this interaction at the peak wave vector, and near magnetic order this small difference changes the height by a large factor. Two-particle self-consistent theory reproduces the peak because its sum rule fixes its single constant interaction near this value, but for n = 0.7-0.9 at T/t = 0.14 its self-energy overestimates the local scattering rate and underestimates the momentum-dependent part. Though strong, the fluctuations are short ranged, with a correlation length of at most about two lattice spacings, and for n = 0.7-0.9 and T/t >= 0.14 the scattering rate near the Fermi surface varies by at most about 1% at fixed band energy, without hot spots. At U/t = 4 dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) reproduces the local scattering rate and quasiparticle weight within a few percent, and the nonlocal part it misses is approximately a function of the band energy. Strong spin fluctuations thus coexist with nearly isotropic quasiparticles, and the results provide a benchmark for extensions of DMFT and for spin-fluctuation theories.

- Computed momentum‑resolved self‑energy and spin susceptibility for doped 3D Hubbard model (n = 4–95, U/t = 4–using connected‑determinant diagrammatic Monte Carlo.
